title: Magnesium Plant, Park Annexation, New Stores
summary:
*   **Wartime Industry Support:** To aid the national defense program, the city agreed to waive its electricity distribution rights, allowing the Lower Colorado River Authority to supply power to a proposed magnesium production plant near Austin.
*   **Major City Expansion:** Significant new territory was annexed, including the Austin Memorial Park property, lands owned by the City and the University of Texas, and the Lake Austin Metropolitan Park.
*   **New Commercial Development:** A permit was granted for a drive-in gasoline filling station, with detailed conditions for its construction and operation, and permission was given for new gas main installations on several streets.
*   **Property and Tax Management:** The city finalized the sale of property it acquired through tax foreclosure and approved the remission of penalties and partial interest on overdue city taxes for multiple property owners.

The following resolution was introduced:
(RESOLUTION)
Statement
The City Council of the City of Austin has been notified by the Lower Colorado River
Authority that the Authority is negotiating with representatives of the United States
Government and representatives of private interests for the location, probably within ten
miles of the City of Austin, of a large industrial plant for the processing and production
of magnesium, a highly important commodity in the National Defense Program.
The Authority has informed the City that it has tentatively agreed to furnish electric
power and energy for such a plant, but must do so in compliance with and subject to the
provisions of a lease and agreement dated February 5, 1936, entered into by and between
the City of Austin and the Authority, under the terms of which the Authority may not
distribute or sell power or electric energy within the limits of the City of Austin or
within the sone lying within ten miles of the corporate limits of the City, except in
certain instances requiring a waiver on the part of the City of Austin of its right to
sell and distribute electric energy and power within' such sone.
With its vast generating capacity, the Lower Colorado River Authority is fully equipped to
furnish adequate power and energy for the operation of such a plant, and it is deemed
advisable and beneficial, not only to the City of Austin, but to the Nation as well, that
every ald be given to the location, development and operation of such a plant because of
its importance in the National Defense Program and its permanent value to the prosperity
and security of the country as a whole, and to assist the Authority in ite commendable
endeavor to bring to this area valuable industry and key projects for the safety of the
American people; therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE OITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTINE That
the City of Austin will, pursuant to appropriate formal requests in accordance with the
terms of the contract of February 5, 1938, waive the City's right to distribute and sell
power and electric energy to the proposed magnesium plant, in the ovent such plant should
be located within ten miles of the corporate limits of the O1ty, and in waiving its right
to sell such power and energy, the Oity of Austin w112 willingly yield to the Lower
Colorado River Authority the right to soll and distribute electric energy and power to the
proposed magnesium processing plant within the ten mile zone described in such contract.
